title: The Free Reduction Band a Long-Standing Catering Client's Order Carries
content:
A client of long standing who orders often is allowed a wider margin on guest numbers than the printed band. The free reduction band standing on an order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is set from the age of the agreement and its delivery record over the 12 months ending on the day notice is given.

| The agreement has run for | Deliveries carried in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given | The free reduction band standing on the order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24 months (two years) or more | 6 or more | twice — 2 times — the free reduction band printed against the catering service level |
| At least 12 months (a year) and fewer than 24 months | 3 or more | one and a half times — 1.5 times — the free reduction band printed against the catering service level |
| Any other case | — | the free reduction band printed against the catering service level |

Each row asks for both of its conditions together. An agreement of 30 months carrying 4 deliveries in those 12 months meets the age of the first row but not its delivery count, and it does not meet the age of the second row either, so its band is the band printed against the service level. An agreement of 15 months carrying 9 deliveries in those 12 months is on the second row, the age condition of the first being unmet.

### Both sides of the counts

On a hypothetical Corporate Catering Service Agreement whose service level is printed with a free reduction band of 8.0 per cent:

- 24 months in force with exactly 6 deliveries in those 12 months gives a band of 16.0 per cent; 24 months with 5 deliveries gives 8.0 per cent, no row being met;
- exactly 12 months in force with exactly 3 deliveries gives 12.0 per cent; 11 months with 8 deliveries gives 8.0 per cent;
- 23 months with 7 deliveries gives 12.0 per cent, the agreement having reached 12 months but not 24.

The age of the agreement is counted from the day it started to the day notice is given, and the delivery count is taken from the delivery entries standing in that agreement's order history over the 12 months ending on that day.
